title: Coherence characterizes constructible finite-module sheaves on vanishing topoi
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $V_f$ [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Then $F$ is constructible in the finite-stratification sense of [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf] if and only if its underlying sheaf of sets $|F|$ is a coherent object of $V_f$ in the sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Author draft, §8.1, printed pp. 17–18, agreement of constructibility and coherence for oriented products, with the finite constant-module variant; finite-presentation Noetherian specialization. Read online; local archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Put $A=|F|$. The coherence/constructibility criterion for the underlying sheaf of sets, [lem-trf-coherent-set-criterion], applies because $S$ is Noetherian, $f$ is of finite presentation, and $V_f$ is the vanishing topos of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. It identifies coherence of $A$ with the existence of finite constructible stratifications of $X$ and $S$ on whose oriented products $A$ is locally constant with finite set values.

source.place: Author draft, §8.1, printed pp. 17–18, set-valued coherence criterion for oriented products

proof.text: Assume $F$ is constructible in the sense of [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf], with strata $X_\alpha$, $S_\beta$. By [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] the module inverse image along $P_{\alpha\beta}\to V_f$ is the ordinary inverse image with the induced operations, so the underlying sheaf of sets of the restriction of $F$ is the restriction of $A$; likewise the underlying sheaf of sets of a constant module sheaf $\underline{M_i}$ is the constant sheaf on the set $M_i$ (forgetting the operations commutes with sheafification). Hence each witnessing isomorphism of module sheaves on $P_{\alpha\beta}/U_i$ gives an isomorphism of $A$ restricted there with the constant sheaf on the finite set $M_i$. These are exactly the witnesses required in [lem-trf-coherent-set-criterion], whose "if" direction (Step 1) gives that $A$ is coherent.

source.place: Author draft, §8.1, printed pp. 17–18, finite-module specialization of the set-valued criterion

proof.text: Conversely assume $A$ is coherent. By [lem-trf-coherent-set-criterion] (Step 1) there are finite constructible stratifications $X_\alpha$, $S_\beta$ and, for each $\alpha,\beta$, a covering family $(U_i)$ of the final object of $P_{\alpha\beta}$ with isomorphisms $\phi_i$ from the restriction of $A$ to $P_{\alpha\beta}/U_i$ onto the constant sheaf $\underline{M_i}$ on a finite set $M_i$. As in Step 2 the restriction $G$ of $F$ to $P_{\alpha\beta}$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with underlying sheaf of sets the restriction of $A$. Fix $i$. Through $\phi_i$ the addition $G\times G\to G$, the zero $1\to G$ and, for each of the finitely many $\lambda\in\Lambda$, the multiplication $\lambda:G\to G$ become morphisms of sheaves $\underline{M_i}\times\underline{M_i}\to\underline{M_i}$, $1\to\underline{M_i}$, $\underline{M_i}\to\underline{M_i}$ on $P_{\alpha\beta}/U_i$. In any topos the constant sheaf on a finite set $N$ is the coproduct $\coprod_{n\in N}1$, coproducts are disjoint and stable under pullback, and $\underline{N}\times\underline{N'}=\underline{N\times N'}$; so a morphism $\underline{N}\to\underline{N'}$ over $U_i$ is the same as a section of $\underline{\operatorname{Map}(N,N')}$ over $U_i$, i.e. a decomposition $U_i=\coprod_{\sigma}U_{i,\sigma}$ indexed by the finite set of maps $\sigma:N\to N'$ such that over $U_{i,\sigma}$ the morphism is the constant one $\underline{\sigma}$. Taking the common refinement of the decompositions for the finitely many operations listed, we get a finite cover $U_i=\coprod_kU_{i,k}$ such that over each $U_{i,k}$ every operation is constant, given by maps $+_k:M_i\times M_i\to M_i$, $0_k\in M_i$, $\lambda_k:M_i\to M_i$. If $U_{i,k}$ is not initial, two constant morphisms $\underline\sigma,\underline\tau:\underline N\to\underline{N'}$ that agree over $U_{i,k}$ have $\sigma=\tau$: if $\sigma(n)\neq\tau(n)$, the section $n$ composed with them lands over $U_{i,k}$ in two disjoint summands of $\coprod_{n'}1$, so $U_{i,k}$ maps to their pullback, which is initial, and hence is initial. The module axioms for $G$ are equalities of morphisms built from these operations, so they hold for the maps $+_k,0_k,\lambda_k$; so $(M_i,+_k,0_k,\lambda_k)$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module $M_{i,k}$ and $\phi_i$ restricted to $U_{i,k}$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-module sheaves $G|_{U_{i,k}}\cong\underline{M_{i,k}}$ (initial $U_{i,k}$ may be discarded or given any module). The family $(U_{i,k})$ still covers the final object of $P_{\alpha\beta}$. Thus each restriction of $F$ is locally constant with finite $\Lambda$-module values on the same strata, which is exactly constructibility in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf].
